pages.text:
I build, operate and explain complex technical systems.

I’m an AI Forward Deployed Engineer, consultant and educator with data and software experience since 2012. My work covers enterprise data platforms, applied AI, cloud infrastructure and the release and support practices that keep them useful.

How I got here

I began in data analysis and backend systems in 2012. Since then, I have worked through enterprise data science, consulting, regulated-data engineering, business intelligence, platform operations and AI system delivery.

The job has expanded with each role. I can move from an architecture discussion into Python or SQL, trace a failing pipeline, review access boundaries, repair a release workflow and explain the trade-offs to stakeholders who do not share the same technical vocabulary.

I work independently when a problem needs concentrated ownership. In enterprise environments, I collaborate with engineering, security, product, domain and governance teams because those systems require more than one point of view.

Read the career timeline

Teaching changed my engineering

I have taught graduate statistics, data visualization, dashboards and real-time Python APIs. I have also led workforce programs in data science and data engineering, and organized developer workshops through Google Developer Groups.

A classroom exposes weak explanations quickly. That experience taught me to document decisions, make operating assumptions visible and leave enough context for the next person to understand a system.

See my teaching work

How I approach the work
Start with the operational problem and the team that will own the result.
Choose the simplest architecture that meets the actual constraints.
Design access control, monitoring and failure handling with the main workflow.
Evaluate model output against representative tasks and known failure cases.
Document decisions so another engineer can operate the system.
What I’m studying now

I started experimenting with software and web technology in 2004. These days I spend that curiosity on self-hosted models, developer tools, distributed systems, cloud economics and the boundary between automated work and human approval.

I direct commercial consulting through Vriksh Consulting Services Inc. This website remains my personal professional record.

Rajadharma

Choose with care

Discover characters, earn deeds and collect relics. Compare your reigns in your local dynasty records.

Professional experience

November 2021–present

AI and data engineering engagements

Vriksh Consulting Services Inc. · Consulting entity

I own architecture, implementation and production support across AI and data engagements. This includes eighteen months owning architecture and production delivery for an enterprise AI assistant. Other platform work includes multi-terabyte datasets and hundreds of automated pipelines; that scale describes the estates I worked on, rather than a measured improvement from my contribution.

January–November 2021

Quality & Technical Services Manager / Lead R&D Data Scientist

Sofvie · Employment

I led technical quality and applied data research, including cloud data workflows and delivery automation.

June 2018–January 2021

Staff Consultant → Senior Consultant

Dentsu / Merkle Cardinal Path · Employment

Staff Consultant, June 2018–January 2020; promoted to Senior Consultant, January 2020–January 2021. My work covered enterprise analytics and cloud data consulting.

March 2017–June 2018

Consultant, Data Science

EY · Employment

I worked on data science and analytical processing for forensic and regulatory work, with client and dataset details kept confidential.

November 2015–March 2017

Data Scientist

Wipro · Employment

I built analytical systems over operational and log data, working on modelling, implementation and performance investigation.

June 2012–November 2015

Early data and software roles

SMART FBO, Hibu and Sigmoid · Grouped early-career period

My early work spanned reporting, backend development and real-time analytics using Python, SQL, R and distributed processing. This grouped period covers several roles.

Teaching and community
Correlation One · 2021–2024 · Lead instructor, Walmart Data Science Bootcamp and DS4A.
Cambrian College · 2020–2024 · Adjunct / Partial Load Professor.
Google Developer Groups · 2020–present · Chapter Lead.
Selected skills

Python, SQL and R; data pipelines and cloud analytics; AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Databricks; AI integration, release automation and production support.

Education

MBA, International Business · ICFAI, Bangalore · 2013–2015.

BE, Information Technology · CMR Institute of Technology, Bangalore · 2007–2012.

pages.text:
Beta
Caffeinate-d

A small native macOS menu-bar wrapper for caffeinate -d, providing a visible toggle for preventing display sleep.

Repository and source download
Scope

Caffeinate-d starts and stops the macOS system command that keeps the display awake. It is intentionally limited to this menu-bar interaction and does not claim broader power-management control.

Release state: the repository declares source version 0.2.0. GitHub does not currently provide a matching packaged release or signed binary download.
Project facts
Platform
macOS
Implementation
Native Swift
Version
Source version 0.2.0
Licence
MIT
Install
Clone the repository and build the Xcode project from source.
Privacy

The application is designed to invoke the local macOS power-management command. The source does not require an account or remote service. This statement applies to the published source and should be reviewed again for every packaged release.

Build from source

Clone the repository on macOS, open its Xcode project and run the application. Use the menu-bar toggle to start or stop display-sleep prevention.
